content: Chloramphenicol interacts with various drugs by influencing the metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4 and CYP2C19. These interactions can lead to increased drug levels, enhanced effects, or heightened toxicity, necessitating careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or avoidance of co-administration. Below are the specific interactions and recommendations: 1. Ritonavir: Chloramphenicol increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 2. Chloramphenicol and Ruxolitinib: Chloramphenicol increases ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce ruxolitinib dosage in patients with myelofibrosis or polycythemia vera. No dose adjustment is needed for graft-versus-host disease. 3. Saxagliptin: Chloramphenicol increases saxagliptin levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Selumetinib: Chloramphenicol increases selumetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce selumetinib dosage and resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 5. Sildenafil: Chloramphenicol increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Siponimod: Chloramphenicol increases siponimod levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid combining siponimod with moderate or strong CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 inhibitors. 7. Sirolimus: Chloramphenicol increases sirolimus levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Sonidegib: Chloramphenicol increases sonidegib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Sparsentan: Chloramphenicol increases sparsentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration upon resumption. 10. Sufentanil: Chloramphenicol increases sufentanil levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Sunitinib: Chloramphenicol increases sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Suvorexant: Chloramphenicol increases suvorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Tacrolimus: Chloramphenicol increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Tamsulosin: Chloramphenicol increases tamsulosin levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Tazemetostat: Chloramphenicol increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Temsirolimus: Chloramphenicol increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Tezacaftor: Chloramphenicol increases tezacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Tofacitinib: Chloramphenicol increases tofacitinib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Tolterodine: Chloramphenicol increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Tolvaptan: Chloramphenicol increases tolvaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Toremifene: Chloramphenicol increases toremifene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Trabectedin: Chloramphenicol increases trabectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Trazodone: Chloramphenicol increases trazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Chloramphenicol reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Administer the vaccine only after completing antibiotic therapy. 25. Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol (Inhaled): Chloramphenicol increases levels of this combination by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Vemurafenib: Chloramphenicol increases vemurafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Venetoclax: Chloramphenicol increases venetoclax levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated during the ramp-up phase in CLL/SLL patients. Adjust dosage and monitor closely in AML patients. 28. Vilazodone: Chloramphenicol increases vilazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce vilazodone dosage to 20 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Vinblastine: Chloramphenicol increases vinblastine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Vincristine: Chloramphenicol increases vincristine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Vorapaxar: Chloramphenicol increases vorapaxar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Reduce dosage as needed. 67. Levamlodipine: Chloramphenicol increases levamlodipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for hypotension and edema. 68. Limit dosage to 5 mg/day. 71. Lumefantrine: Chloramphenicol increases lumefantrine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Reduce daily dosage. 74. Midazolam (Intranasal): Chloramphenicol increases midazolam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for prolonged sedation. 75. Monitor for adverse effects. 80. Oliceridine: Chloramphenicol increases oliceridine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust dosage and monitor for respiratory depression. 81.
